title: LVM
subtitle: Physical → volume group → logical — flip for meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: LVM stack: physical volumes pooled into a volume group, then sliced into logical volumes
cards.notes: Then mkfs + mount for a real filesystem

cards.meaning: Label a disk/partition as an LVM physical volume
List PVs, which VG they are in, and free space
Pool one or more PVs into a volume group
Create an LV using all remaining space in the VG
Create an LV of a fixed size
List logical volumes (path, size, VG, status)
Format the LV as a filesystem — separate from LVM itself
cards.notes: LVM only gives a block device; then mount (+ fstab for reboot)

cards.meaning: Resize LVs dynamically, pool disks, snapshots, online changes — unlike fixed partitions
cards.notes: Almost Linux-only; Btrfs subvolumes may already be enough flexibility
